reviews.text: While this film features some interesting themes, it’s also methodical, mundane at times and feels like a bunch of random brushstrokes.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: By envisioning a world where the consumers get consumed, the film calls for a reconceptualization of human and nonhuman relationships. “Under the Skin” denies human exceptionalism and supremacy.
reviews.author: Wael Khairy

reviews.text: …any film or streaming version of Faber’s novel would take an Avatar-level budget to produce, and the commercial possibilities would be limited, but Glazer’s sole misstep as a director was to create this absurdly truncated version of this alienating tale…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: [Director Jonathan] Glazer is less interested in the what and the why than in the texture of the experience, the intensity of the imagery, the sense of adaptation and alienation as this alien starts to connect with her victims.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: As a broader take on gender relations, though, Under The Skin is willfully perplexing...
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: Maximal minimalism, of the kind of heightened sensation you’d expect from Jonathan Glazer... His character is the ultimate consumer, shopping for men among the faces on the street, who will be literally taken by desire?
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: It's unquestionably one of the most important science-fiction pictures in recent memory.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Director Jonathan Glazer's intentionally vague and aloof adaptation of Michael Faber's novel devotes its a torturous 108 minutes on the efforts of Scarlett Johansson's seductive alien to lure lonely, unattached men to their death.
reviews.author: Robert Sims

reviews.text: Cinematic Ketamine for the soul
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: With arresting images and hypnotic soundtrack, the film is one of the most singularly mesmerizing movie watching experience I've had in a long time.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: If Johansson had been asked to speak to Glasgow residents in depth about their lives and conditions, their thoughts and feelings, Under the Skin might have had genuine value.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: It deliberately challenges the audience, almost daring them to stay along for the ride, but those brave enough to take the journey will be rewarded with a story that takes a sly look at human identity filtered through the guise of an alien.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: What started off as a potentially feminist film fell into a tired fairytale.
reviews.author: Kjerstin Johnson

reviews.text: It does not develop a plot so much as a fascinating feeling of underlying horror.
reviews.author: Sarah Mirk

reviews.text: The film's curiosities lose out to the weird imperceptibleness of characters and plot.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: A genre oddity of the utmost excellence
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Under the Skin is essentially a road movie abstracted into an erotic poem, where somewhere in between our pleasures and fears coincide.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: For all the qualities it has, I view it as though it were sitting inside of a display case, only allowing me to engage from a distance.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Under the Skin will not only go down in the history of science fiction cinema for its powerful imagery... but also because of how easily it revises the myth of the femme fatale. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergi Sánchez

reviews.text: An exceptional heir to... its literary ancestors like The Man Who Fell to Earth. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: Mica Levi's score deepens [Jonathan] Glazer's gripping visual abstraction, and [Scarlett] Johansson is more than effective as innocent victim and cold, calculating killer.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Haunting and beautiful at the same time, Under The Skin is a cinematic achievement. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Although the odd scene risks ludicrousness (Johansson observing Tommy Cooper like some dumbfounded pet), the impact of Glazer's stylised approach and Levi's hair-raising soundtrack make the film burrow inside your skull.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Glazer and cinematographer Daniel Landin have created a work that is more visually stunning than most films with 10 times Under the Skin's budget.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: A cinematic masterpiece that's surreal, scintillating, and unforgettably strange.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: If a Supreme Court Justice can declare porn to be without definition but knowable on sight, so too can art fall into the same metric. I don't know why Under the Skin is exceptional art. I just know it is.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Under The Skin is for sure an oddity with unscripted dialogue, strange acting, even stranger events, but the alluring monotonous aesthetic accompanied by hypnotizing VFX and a transporting score makes it a definite must-see.
reviews.author: Hanna B

reviews.text: Glazer's hauntingly assured direction, accompanied by Johansson's chilling performance, merge to create something unforgettable.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: While Johansson is great her role is too enigmatic to make any of the final acts resonate.
reviews.author: C.J. Prince

reviews.text: A mesmerising, deeply attentive piece of filmmaking; acutely original in spite of its eminent heraldry.
reviews.author: Cameron Ward

reviews.text: Under the Skin is all about the experience, about soaking up Glazer's otherworldly nightmare like a sponge. His third film is a cinematic anomaly, alien in both its subject matter and form, and it's to be treasured.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: The problem is: Johansson's character knows, from the start of the film how to be, by all appearances, a human woman, and the filmmakers never seem curious how she learned to do so.
reviews.author: Ren Jender

reviews.text: Glazer has not only single-handedly regalvanised the British sci-fi but has also earned the right to be uttered in the same breath as genre greats such as David Cronenberg and Nicolas Roeg.
reviews.author: Daniel Green

reviews.text: It is a challenging role for the actress and she [Scarlett Johansson] rises to it seamlessly.
reviews.author: Paula Fleri-Soler

reviews.text: I won't be recommending this movie to anyone, except insomniacs.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: A film about orientation, or, rather, disorientation, as Glazer seeks to depict how the world might look from alien eyes.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: It's certainly not for everyone, but for those who can stick with it will find an incredibly unique and captivating experience.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: An experience I wrestle with, in a mostly positive way. Contains a lot of tremendous strengths, including an intoxicating score and a lot of blank spaces for the individual viewer to fill with interpretation.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: A lean and absorbing vision of Earth and society as an incomprehensible place.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: No matter what you eventually end up thinking about "Under the Skin," you will very likely find yourself thinking about it for some time.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: It is a Scarlett Johansson movie, but not as we know it.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: It is a film that unwaveringly starts with the absurd, only to end up with an observation that is as simple as it is profound.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: What was originally a bonkers and sententious parable about class, labour, and the horrors of the meat industry-run by a race of talking antelope-like beings from another planet-is now essentially an abstract coming-of-age picture.
reviews.author: Blake Williams

reviews.text: There's an under-explored sociological insight to be gleaned from the encounters that follow.
reviews.author: Jay Kuehner

reviews.text: this mysterious masterpiece seduces you into a very different twilight zone of unforgettable sci-fi strangeness.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Under The Skin is as sloppy as it is bold and may quickly bore some with its evasive themes.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: [Director] Jonathan Glazer's Under the Skin is a film with the courage of its silences and ellipses.
reviews.author: Geoffrey O'Brien

reviews.text: Under the Skin is a movie that truly defies articulation. It's visceral; not violent or exploitative, but challenging and exotic.
reviews.author: Chris Alexander

reviews.text: Glazer judges the men who die as he leers at Johansson in the exact same manner. Then there's a fire, and you wonder why you bothered.
reviews.author: Tara Thorne

reviews.text: I just hated, hated, hated every mind-numbingly pretentious minute of it.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: Though Johansson barely speaks, she conveys her alien character's unfamiliarity with her body and her surroundings, as well as her growing awareness of what it means to be human, in every look and subtle motion.
reviews.author: Erika W. Smith

reviews.text: Repetitive but creepy sci-fi horror flick likely to get under your skin.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: An exploration and subversion of the unstated theme of 'Species' and its ilk: the fear of female sexuality, and the fantasy scenarios that are all tied up in those fears.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Like much of the imagery that follows, the opening segment is a sensory immersion into an experience beyond comprehension.
reviews.author: Zade Constantine

reviews.text: Like so many classics, it works singularly across multiple genres (horror, science fiction, drama, thriller) but its beauty comes from all those elements working in concert.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Minds will be blown to the four winds. And - fair warning - a percentage of American ticket buyers may find themselves exasperated and/or exiting early.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The premise is intriguing and it's only the possibility that something might come of it that keeps your attention, but that attention is never rewarded.
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: A visionary, thought-provoking sci-fi masterpiece ...
reviews.author: John Oursler

reviews.text: There is a relentless quality about it that keeps you going. It's the kind of "art" film that reminds one of Roman Polanski's "Repulsion."
reviews.author: Mal Vincent

reviews.text: Under the Skin is exactly where it gets.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Glacial in pace, skeletal in plot, and generally nasty, Jonathan Glazer's Under the Skin is a repetitive nightmare of drear and dread punctuated by moments of queasy-making horror.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: With a soundtrack of grinding frequencies and uneasy point-of-view camera shots, the everyday becomes otherworldly.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: Under the Skin manages to fulfill the promise of its prologue, burrowing under the viewer's skin without pretense, or the benefit of Laura's bedside manner.
reviews.author: Michelle Orange

reviews.text: We do learn a little about ourselves by the conclusion, but when it came to holding my attention for the duration of a feature-length film, I found the experience far too alien.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: There's an eerie brilliance and a haunting beauty to "Under the Skin," writer-director Jonathan Glazer's beyond-strange exploration of what it means to be human - seen from an outside perspective.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The exquisitely odd "Under the Skin" feels like a really ambitious student film. That has nothing to do with its quality.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: It's admirable that Johansson should be so willing to go off the Hollywood grid, but the truth is, "Under the Skin" would have been a lot better if it wasn't so excruciatingly arty.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Nearly wordless and devoid of comforting context, and driven by composer Mica Levi's haunting and discordant score, Under the Skin will drill deep and lay eggs in your brain.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Like Johansson's unearthly visitor, the film loses its way occasionally, but it's an experience you'll not forget in a hurry.
reviews.author: Andrew Collins

reviews.text: As the movie guesses at her, wants her, is repelled by her, and cannot fathom her, you are left to figure out your own position, under your skin.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: The good news is that Under The Skin does indeed break out of its own formula. The bad news is that it does so in a way that seems to delight in obfuscating its message, and is wilfully, gleefully impenetrable.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: This one will haunt you.
reviews.author: Glenn Sumi

reviews.text: Glazer continues to bat 1.000, which is both good and bad. Good because he makes amazing films, bad because he's only made three in 14 years.
reviews.author: Don R. Lewis

reviews.text: Under the Skin is one of those unforgettable movies that promises to stay with you long after the end credits have rolled.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: This is an intelligent and classy film, part sci-fi, part horror and part thriller that shows just how good an actress Johansson can be when given the chance.
reviews.author: David Edwards

reviews.text: Imagine for a moment that Marilyn Monroe - in a black wig and outfitted in tarty Primark - is dropped into the dreich streets of Glasgow, and drives round in a white van picking up eager young men.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: By estranging us from supposed normality, Glazer forces us to identify with otherness: Johansson's mystery woman is a predator, but also potentially a victim.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The oddest and most frustrating film I've seen all year.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: "Under the Skin" is perfectly fine. I'm just not sure I'll ever see it again unless I have to.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Offering a compelling, alien's-eye view of our murky human world, Under The Skin is dark, edgy, mysterious and very strange, with the most distinctive score since There Will Be Blood chipping away at our nerves.
reviews.author: Graham Young

reviews.text: The lack of clarity is part of the film's appeal. Under the Skin stubbornly refuses to explain itself, letting Johansson's voluptuous body do the talking.
reviews.author: Deborah Kennedy

reviews.text: Under the Skin is a hollow film with a fascinating premise that could have been so much more.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Stunning to behold, often impossible-seeming, hypnotic and profoundly affecting, Under the Skin achieves what some sci-fi films could only ever dream of: actually taking us to another universe entirely.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Under the Skin is moody and strange and mysterious, but ultimately, it's about the human race, about what a dispassionate observer might think of us, if she were seeing us for the first time.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: Glazer has worked an extended thread of extremely earthbound vérité footage into a film that tells the most outré intergalactic story.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Glazer's Sexy Beast and Birth were idiosyncratic but Under The Skin trumps them triumphantly, being compelling, weird, intensely disturbing and ultimately bizarrely moving. Many of its images are shockingly vivid for me two weeks after having seen it.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Being forced to engage with the material just to try and make sense of what we're seeing is part of what makes this so compelling.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Johansson is brave and memorable and, though you may at times wonder what on earth's going on, Under the Skin may just get under your skin.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: A fantastic mind-game of a movie with an uneering sense of how to keep viewers off-balance, Under the Skin is an intriguing, subtle, sci-fi head-scratcher designed to have you guessing - in the best possible way - about just what the heck is going on.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: A cold, disturbing, impenetrable piece of filmmaking, it's a movie that will understandably alienate mainstream audiences, even as it carves a place for itself as a modern-day cult classic.
reviews.author: Tom Clift

reviews.text: A nonsensical and impenetrable scenario that intrigues as a sensory experience with an alien seductress as our guide but frustrates in the final analysis.
reviews.author: Urban Cinefile Critics

reviews.text: I found it really interesting, really beautiful. I'm giving it three stars because I didn't understand it.
reviews.author: Margaret Pomeranz

reviews.text: As a sensory experience, Under the Skin often astounds.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: Instigante ao criar imagens evocativas, sugerir subtextos complexos, investir em metáforas e alegorias.
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Writer/director Jonathan Glazer's art-house sci-fi allegory Under the Skin slips up on the viewer so surreptitiously that the pull of its final 30 minutes comes as a bit of a shock.
reviews.author: Nathan Southern

reviews.text: "Under the Skin" is so baffling and riveting that when a reel was skipped the first time I saw it I never batted an eye.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: There are images in this film unlike any I've seen before.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: ...one of the most aggressively arty (and often downright inaccessible) films to come around in ages...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: If you're looking for a solid, mainstream movie that's easily understood and appreciated ... you'd better stop reading right now.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: All this is initially fascinating, and then progressively less so.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: You can feel the cold. That's the simplest way to explain Jonathan Glazer's success with Under the Skin.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Skin always is moving, but slowly, thoughtfully, positioning both Glazer's camera and the alien as observers.
reviews.author: Carla Meyer

reviews.text: A film about perception, about how our eyes interpret images of light for our brains, and how we apply meaning to them, be they horrifying, or beautiful, or both.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The result is a freshly minted cult masterpiece, mixing the wonder (and, yes, the occasional slowness) of 2001: A Space Odyssey with the terror of Alien.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: A Thinking Person's Horror Film.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Most of Under the Skin operates on an almost subconscious level. The truth is out there in Glazer's screenplay, which he co-wrote with Walter Campbell, but it's intuitive rather than didactic.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: This is the most confident and bold kind of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Predatory brainy fantasy film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Aptly named, it feels otherworldly. It explores the the difference between simply being sentient and actually becoming sympathetic. As a moviegoing experience, it is thrillingly alive, hearkening back to the heyday of '70s art cinema.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: Aims to be mysterious but merely comes off as monotonous...the sort of film that should have the word 'cult' stamped onto the canisters containing the reels.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Under the Skin doesn't just affirm the movies' ability to draw us out of our worldview: it raises the bar. I can't wait to watch it five or six more times, at least.
reviews.author: Rob Humanick

reviews.text: Glazer struggles to add plot to his formula within the confines of his languid, almost underwater pacing, and some scenes fall flat as a result.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: ...I feel something like a man who has had a close encounter with something beautiful, dangerous and beyond my comprehension. It's the sort of movie on which cult reputations are made.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: Early in the film, the woman plucks an ant from a body, and the moviegoer at times may feel as uncomprehending as that insect, while the Johansson character might as well be an alien entomologist, observing the strange hive culture of humanity.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: A uniquely surreal and understated film... Unnverving, unforgettable.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Avoids the adrenalin-junkie tactics of most sci-fi ... [but it] could have taken us to more interesting places. Glazer's too preoccupied with his bait-and-devour scenario.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Subtly strange and surreal, appealing to avant-garde art-house audiences searching for something different.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A claustrophobically seamless and unnerving drama of self-awakening.
reviews.author: Nicolas Rapold

reviews.text: It's a cold bath of sight and sound, shrouded in a dense fog (literally/metaphorically).
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: "Yes, it's the 'Scarlett Johansson naked alien movie,' although its much deeper and smarter than that formulation makes it sound
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: For cinephiles that enjoy artistic debate more than concrete answers, Under the Skin provides an intriguing platform for discussion and reflection.
reviews.author: Ben Kendrick

reviews.text: Serious, intriguing, but lacking a human core
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A fascinating mystery that works emotionally and visually
reviews.author: Marty Mapes

reviews.text: Scarlett Johansson goes spare and bare.
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: This is a movie about alienation that drives home its point with real aliens.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: A direct descendant of Nicolas Roeg's classic "The Man Who Fell to Earth," "Under the Skin" is the kind of movie people will be talking about, and dissecting and puzzling over, for years.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: Visually stunning but virtually indecipherable ...
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Under the Skin definitely gets under your skin.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: A deeply atmospheric and thrillingly unconventional movie, one that is unlike any I can recall.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: A cinematic happening near-guaranteed to get under your skin and into your head for far longer than is comfortable.
reviews.author: Marc Savlov

reviews.text: Johansson cuts a fascinatingly distant figure.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: The story is at once simple and impenetrable. Visually it is arresting, when it isn't murky, and the droning, atonal soundtrack is as perfect for the film as it is annoying.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: This arty sci-fi thriller, adapted from a 2000 novel by Michael Faber, raises far more questions than it answers, yet that enigmatic quality is central to its appeal.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: You'll be captivated or irritated, depending on your need for a clear, linear narrative.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: ...longs for a world where what we look like - whether we're beautiful or ugly - no longer dominates who we are.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: It's a film that forces us to consider what the complicated surfaces of humanity really cover up. The answer is both beautiful and awful to behold.
reviews.author: Jeff Meyers

reviews.text: Scarlett Johansson mesmerizes as an alien who becomes intrigued by her prey-us.
reviews.author: Alynda Wheat

reviews.text: Both a naturalistic work of science fiction and a feminist masterpiece, this uncompromising and often brilliant work of cinema is occasionally hard to figure out but impossible to ignore.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: I loved it. Dazzling, erotic and electrifying. Johansson is fantastic and the mood and music thrilling.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: It does a very good job of what it sets out to do. The question is whether or not I really care about what it does. Therein lies the problem. I don't think I really do.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: A formalist masterwork: moody, meditative and mystifying.
reviews.author: Sam Fragoso

reviews.text: For all its qualities, Under the Skin ultimately frustrates.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: "Under the Skin" clearly does not intend to telegraph its meaning, but meaning may not be the movie's strong suit.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: An unnerving, disturbing, utterly disorienting encounter with something wholly other.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: As avant garde in execution as any narrative film I can think of.
reviews.author: Bryant Frazer

reviews.text: ...as incomprehensible as 'Last Year at Marienbad' but not nearly as good.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: This haunting, provocative film is the essence of what it means to call a work of art "adult,"because of the way it presents and engages with the material.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: "Mr. Glazer is attempting something powerful and unusual in cinema, a visually-aurally told story."
reviews.author: D.K. Holm

reviews.text: It's a slow burn with very little happening throughout. However, there's a lot going on under the skin, if you will.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Those that are able to slip under its spell will enjoy one of the most striking theatrical experiences this year.
reviews.author: Bryan Bishop

reviews.text: Sexy beast, indeed. Johansson lures men to gruesome death in moody art film, sci-fi/horror hybrid. Entrancing.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Glazer adopts a muddied, overly subdued tone, both visually and narratively, which drains "Under the Skin" of nearly all life.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: The protagonist's process repeats itself over and over again, and each time ... we're simultaneously certain of and baffled by the whole thing.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Glazer's unwillingness to spell out everything about this strange and mesmerizing film; is part of what makes it so compelling and at times infuriating.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A discordant, off-putting, psychosexual science fiction piece that features a daring turn from Scarlett Johansson, but one that will leave many audience members scratching their heads.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: Once "Under the Skin" reaches its surprisingly affecting conclusion, it feels less like a cinematic novel than a well-executed short story.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: At the risk of classifying a work so thrillingly unclassifiable in its unrivaled vision, "Under the Skin" is an instantaneously quintessential 21st-century masterpiece in science-fiction and horror.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: "Under the Skin" begins to take on the feel of tragedy; of a creature trapped, like that baby, somewhere it cannot survive.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The movie's a cinematic Rubik's Cube that snaps together surprisingly easily, yet whose larger meanings remain tantalizingly out of reach.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The haunting other worldliness of "Under the Skin" gets, well, under your skin.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: This becomes quite dull, even sleep-inducing, especially considering the movie's overall cast of slow-moving gloom.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Whatever you think the movie means, its most important element is clearly Johansson's performance, which is simultaneously bold and subtle.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Plunges sci-fi into narrative limbo and visual liquidity.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: It's not a film for everyone, but Under the Skin has a unique aura about it that's fascinating, even if the final cut seems engineered to be a merciless test of patience.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Scarlett Johansson is an alien serial killer who sexes men to death in a misogynist fanboy wet dream that also fails to satisfy as science fiction.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: It stayed true to itself, and while "Under the Skin" isn't for everyone, it's nevertheless an artistic achievement that is worth exploring below the surface.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: It may turn some viewers off, but "Under the Skin" is a worthwhile new take on the classic horror premise of body-snatching.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: It's as existential as a sci-fi/horror film can possibly be. It requires that the viewer slip into a meditative mood and remain there for more than 90 minutes.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Pondering the questions, reveling in the mysteries - that's what matters. And I haven't even said the words naked Scarlett Johansson yet.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Under the Skin, even through its more uneventful segments, is still a ripping and compelling intellectual provocation.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: I was willing to watch more to discover what was underneath the surface. Once I found out, I was frozen in place, and then Scarlett Johansson and Jonathan Glazer had their way with me.
reviews.author: Dan Kois

reviews.text: Visually sumptuous but inconsistently intriguing, Glazer's science-fiction film skillfully boils down genre tropes to their visceral essence, but simultaneously reduces an emotionally resonant narrative to an obtuse series of vignettes.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: If you've seen an experimental film or three...then there's nothing here that's going to drive you to reconsider what cinema can be. But Under the Skin still feels the work of a radical.
reviews.author: Jake Mulligan

reviews.text: It's bleak and difficult to watch at times - certainly not traditional escapist fare - yet also intellectually challenging and visually stimulating for those with patience.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: At times the film is right on the border between mesmerizing and narcotizing, but it casts an otherworldly spell.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Johansson has to be at once achingly specific and so general that you can hang all manner of symbols on her. Somehow she pulls it off.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: This visionary science fiction film is haunting and the best new release I've seen so far in 2014.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Glazer's made an icy thriller of ontological and existential proportions. What does it mean to be human, to be alive? In Johansson he has a star who doesn't fear being a repository of those questions.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: Watching this film feels like a genesis moment - of sci-fi fable, of filmmaking, of performance - with all the ambiguity and excitement that implies.
reviews.author: Betsy Sharkey

reviews.text: One of the many startling things about "Under the Skin" is how complicated and distressing a story can be told with almost no dialogue and absolutely no explanation or back story.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: The movie's eerie, climactic image challenges our conventional notions of human identity and leaves us reflecting on the possibility that every being in the universe is an alien in disguise.
reviews.author: Stephen Holden

reviews.text: So unfathomable that it feels like a dully haunting nightmare whose details retreat and fade almost immediately upon waking.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: 'Under the Skin' sometimes feels like it should be more elusive, but the moment you try and lock it down it slips away from you, going off into weirder territory.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: Jonathan Glazer's "Under the Skin" holds you in a state of suspense tinged with dread from the very first image on the screen.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Beautifully eerie, yet disappointingly dull ...
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: It's a rare feat for a film to successfully convey the voice of the Other. Especially when that voice is an Other to everyone else here on Earth.
reviews.author: Scott Wold

reviews.text: A siren from another planet appears in Glasgow, Scotland on a special mission that challenges her sexual allure and desires.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The lack of context - who she is, why she's here - has the thrillingly uncomfortable effect of making us just as attuned to the strangeness of everyday minutiae as she is.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: Johansson is phenomenal in every sense of the word. She joins Glazer in creating a brave experiment in cinema that richly rewards the demands it makes. The result is an amazement, a film of beauty and shocking gravity.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Glazer's meticulously reality-cracking mannerisms and Johansson's glassy watchfulness make for shivering visuals but nearly muffle the film completely. But those concluding stretches...help this elegant mystery of existence regain a dark purpose.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: Under the Skin falls in love with its bleak monotony. It is a melodrama with all the thrills surgically excised.
reviews.author: Richard Corliss

reviews.text: Under The Skin lets its nightmarish imagery do the talking, forgoing explanation in favor of total sensory immersion.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Dream girl Scarlett Johansson digs for oil and hits a dry hole in Under the Skin.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: A rather shapeless film where what's happening onscreen is often less interesting than trying to figure out whether the participants recognize they're sharing the cab of a truck with a world-famous actress.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: Johansson provides an extraordinary window into an alien being; through her eyes, we see and hear the world as someone not from here would. Her performance is the payoff that makes Glazer's enigmatic storytelling choices so effective.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Wholly original and awe inspiring. "Under the Skin" is a visually stunning comment on our obsession with a celebrity's body.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: There are dozens of mysteries in Under the Skin that don't cohere in any logical way but work like gangbusters on the imaginative subconscious.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: When you wake up from this odd dream, you may wonder what the point was. It's probably there, but it's lost in that dark fog.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: A quiet, moody sci-fi tale..has an experimental feel and gives up few of its secrets without a struggle.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: This is a movie that at its most sensitive is about loneliness, and at its bleakest and most searching is a look at the mechanics of sexual predation.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: [VIDEO ESSAY] Scarlett Johansson makes for one attractive hot-and-cold alien ice queen, but seduction and murder is all she has on her mind.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Glazer is nothing if not ambitious; the rough edge of naturalism, on the streets, slices into the more controlled and stylized look of science fiction, and the result seems both to drift and to gather to a point of almost painful intensity.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Throughout, what truly matters to director Jonathan Glazer is articulating through visual and aural enticement the unconscious power of our death drive.
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: From the disorienting opening frames, music video director Glazer's first feature film in a decade is clearly more akin to the provocative Birth than his 2000 paeon to kinetic violence, Sexy Beast.
reviews.author: Anne Thompson

reviews.text: Even in a black wig and ratty fake-fur coat, Scarlett Johansson's otherworldly allure is intact, confirming any suspicions you may have that Hollywood stars belong to another species.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Under the Skin gets under the skin. It is an experience that has as much to do with hypnosis as with cinema.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: A striking attempt to tell an exotic story in a down-to-earth environment that deserves praise for its singularity of vision, even as it runs the risk of ridicule.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A masterclass in technique.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: It's perhaps best to consider Glazer's film to be an avant garde midnight movie, using familiar genre conventions to explore conceptual philosophical ideas.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: Scarlett Johansson is disturbingly good at playing an alien in human form, without any special effects.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: What is captivating about this film is the convincing way it presents our own familiar, prosaic world.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Scarlett Johansson goes off the radar in this low-budget Scottish thriller, which is far more offbeat than anything she's ever done before.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: A rare example of filmmaking with unwavering vision, and one that will burrow its way under your skin for quite some time.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: So rigorous and singular is Glazer's technique that it is hard to believe the film will not register with future audiences as a classic of its era.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Although Under the Skin screams allegory, it's hard to see for what.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: For all its clinical detachment, Glazer's film becomes its own oblique treatise on what it means to be and feel human.
reviews.author: Samuel Wigley

reviews.text: You could find its entrancements stalking you for good, in every meaning of that phrase.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: It sure as hell got under mine.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: It didn't get under my skin, just on my nerves.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: Few films will linger with you like this one does.
reviews.author: Violet Lucca

reviews.text: Jonathan Glazer's loose adaptation of Michel Faber's novel tightens its hellish grip thanks in no small measure to Mica Levi's shuddering electronic score ...
reviews.author: Tim Evans

reviews.text: Extraordinary sci-fi thriller, at once haunting, hypnotic and deeply disturbing, thanks to stunning cinematography, a chilling soundtrack and an instantly iconic performance from Scarlett Johansson that is nothing less than astonishing.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: An utterly beguiling retracing of the word glamour back to its witchy origins.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: With his first film in close to a decade, Glazer has created a captivating nightmare, a heady, haunting experience that demands multiple viewings.
reviews.author: Emma Dibdin

reviews.text: Under The Skin finds grace even in moments of raw horror, composed by a filmmaker who can legitimately call himself a master of the art.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: In refusing to spoon-feed the audience information, Glazer's film instead burrows into the brain, the ambiguous nature of proceedings making it all-the-more beguiling. The result is a film that's hard to shake after the credits have rolled.
reviews.author: Chris Tilly

reviews.text: Eventually I was too bored to care.
reviews.author: Siobhan Synnot

reviews.text: Odd and sexy, troubling and touching, frustrating and mesmerising, dull and haunting.
reviews.author: Nev Pierce

reviews.text: You may not be sure what you've seen, but you've sure seen something.
reviews.author: Andrew Lowry

reviews.text: If you let it, Under the Skin will stay under yours for years to come.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: What begins as an eerie psychosexual horror movie slowly shifts to a haunting study of loneliness and female subjugation.
reviews.author: Jamie Dunn

reviews.text: A genuinely unique, full-on sensory experience that treads its own path between narrative clarity and pure visual expression. It is a film that will leave audiences dazed, disturbed and full of questions about what they have experienced.
reviews.author: Paul Gallagher

reviews.text: Depicts a warped path of self-understanding in which people (especially women) realize sex has been externalized into something that can be wielded.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: Disorientating, disturbing, weirdly funny in places, and confounding in others, it's a true original.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The most striking passages deliver a heartily Kubrickian dose of science-fiction erotica but the movie's menacing allure evaporates midway through, followed by the last vestiges of a comprehensible plotline.
reviews.author: Jason Anderson

reviews.text: The film undeniably deconstructs female sexuality in relation to masculine power, and the baffling nature of that relationship, which is unraveled via the perspective of an alien.
reviews.author: Tina Hassannia

reviews.text: This is hardly the first film to observe an alien encountering strange customs, but it may be the first that seems conceived from that perspective formally as well as dramatically.
reviews.author: Ben Kenigsberg

reviews.text: Under The Skin is an exercise in identifying with the unknowable, and its ultimate conclusion is that while some acclimation is attainable, it's never a clean fit.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Glazer certainly has managed to make one of the most outlandish portraits of alienation in recent memory. "Under the Skin," no matter its faults, certainly will get under yours.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Frustrating but occasionally brilliant. Some arresting visuals.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Viewers willing to embrace a purely visual experience without dramatic, emotional or psychological substance will comprise an ardent cheering section, but the film provides too little for even relatively adventurous specialized audiences to latch onto ...
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: ...a creepy little sci-fi thinker that burrows itself underneath your skin and tests the way you perceive sexuality.
reviews.author: Erik Davis

reviews.text: Under the Skin may be a challenge to make sense of and connect with, but thanks to many gorgeous and haunting sequences, it proves equally difficult to forget.
reviews.author: Darren Ruecker

reviews.text: We don't get totally in her head, but it is still rewarding to stay in your own and watch.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: An undeniably ambitious but ultimately torpid and silly tale of an alien on the prowl.
reviews.author: Scott Foundas

reviews.text: There are echoes of the end of 2001: A Space Odyssey in this and in the observational alien tale The Man Who Fell To Earth. The comparisons do Glazer no favours.
reviews.author: Kaleem Aftab

reviews.text: It's hard to instantly come down on either side of the fence for this film. It's so defiantly clinical and furtive that, even though it's clearly a work of great substance and mystery, it lacks a basic sense of tenderness.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Glazer may be the visionary behind "Under the Skin" cinematic highs, but it must be noted that this film lives and dies on Johansson's incredible turn.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: There is latent, pregnant energy in this picture, a thrum of dread that underlays every frame.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: This is a brave and fascinating film that is at once surreal yet depicts a world we know all too well.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: A sometimes hypnotically beautiful, sometimes monotonous sci-fi experiment.
reviews.author: Jon Frosch

reviews.text: An intoxicating marvel, strange and sublime.
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: This is a mysterious, eerie, experience, whose resistance to easy interpretation (and freewheeling approach to source material) has something of Tarkovsky about it.
reviews.author: Lee Marshall

reviews.text: It works with very little in the way of a screenplay and even less obvious explanation - but with a sense of mystery and wonder that a good film-maker can manufacture through style and atmosphere.
reviews.author: Derek Malcolm

reviews.text: A story that plays as a kind of malarial dream, bathed in cold sweat and seeing hallucinations in every corner.
reviews.author: Xan Brooks

reviews.text: Amid its scorching, fractured images, one certainty is brought into crisp focus. This is, very simply and straightforwardly, a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: What we used to call a 'visionary achievement' -- mesmerizing nightmare fuel in the vein of vintage Cronenberg, with the same sleek, disorienting gloss that Glazer put on his extraordinary 'Birth.'
reviews.author: Eugene Novikov

reviews.text: Picture a sister film to "The Man Who Fell to Earth." Glazer shares Nicolas Roeg's taste in elliptical storytelling and interplanetary tragedy, arriving at something you could almost call horror with a heart.
reviews.author: Chris Willman

reviews.text: A deliberately oblique work that prizes textures above answers.
reviews.author: William Goss

synopsis: Disguising herself as a human female, an extraterrestrial (Scarlett Johansson) drives around Scotland and tries to lure unsuspecting men into her van.
